Subject: TIA scope for multi-region inference (US/EU/UK)

Hi Nikhil,

Quick intro — I'm Simon, Legal Ops at HelixAI. We're finalizing our DPA and need to verify the transfer safeguards for a multi-region inference deployment pattern: EU origin -> Redwood hosted inference (eu-west) with optional US fallback and a UK-specific addendum for some customers.

Can you share a checklist of the TIA (or DTIA) artifacts you can provide, plus the expected timeline to produce them? Specifically we need:
- a mapping between SCC modules (and the UK IDTA/UK Addendum) and Redwood controls,
- subprocessor residency list and whether any subprocessors process EU data in the US,
- onshore cache fallback design (how data flows when routed to the US), and
- HSM/KMS custody model and SOC2 attestation references.

If you can also confirm which artifacts are final and which are projected, that helps legal signoff cadence. Happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Simon
Legal Ops, HelixAI

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (security/ops) who will own the artifacts. High-level plan below and I attached our starting checklist.

What we can supply (short):
- SCC/UK IDTA mapping matrix that shows clause-to-control mapping (final except where dependent on customer-specific routing).
- Subprocessor CSV with residency and processing locale (snapshot + weekly refresh).
- Infrastructure diagram + onshore-cache fallback narrative (draft; finalized after small ops validation run).
- KMS/HSM custodial note and SOC2 report excerpt (final).

Proposed delivery timeline:
- Day 0 (today): checklist + request for any Helix-specific routing examples (attached).
- Day 3: subprocessor CSV + SCC/IDTA mapping (first pass).
- Day 7: infrastructure diagram + onshore-cache fallback design (ops review).
- Day 10: consolidated zip (TIA-evidence-sprint.zip) with signed attestation language for DPA.

If that works, Kimberly will confirm the legal language for the UK Addendum and whether we need a bespoke rider for caching fallback.

Thanks — I'll book a 30-min alignment if helpful.

Best,

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: TIA scope for multi-region inference (US/EU/UK) — mapping and required artifacts

Simon / Nikhil — thanks. Quick legal/controls summary and concrete list of deliverables we will provide for HelixAI. I'm keeping items pragmatic so Helix can push to procurement quickly.

What Redwood will include for the TIA/DTIA and UK Addendum package (deliverables):
1) SCC/IDTA matrix (PDF) — maps each SCC module paragraph to Redwood controls and the artifact that demonstrates it (e.g., logging: trace sample + retention policy). Status: final for hosted runtime; note: routing-specific controls flagged as "depends on final routing policy".
2) Subprocessor registry (CSV) — fields: name, role, region, data residency, legal base (SCC/UK Addendum), contact. Status: snapshot (will include weekly cadence). [attachment stub: subprocessor-csv.csv]
3) Site processing map (PDF) — diagram of EU region -> eu-west inference cluster -> optional US fallback -> onshore-cache fallback narrative (how we shard cache and clear KV on crossover). Status: draft; ops must validate. [attachment stub: site-processing-map.pdf]
4) SOC 2 Type II excerpt & KMS attestation (PDF) — redacted copies we provide under NDA for procurement. Status: final (standard excerpt).
5) TIA evidence sprint bundle (zip) — consolidated folder of the above + redwood attestation letter. Expected delivery Day 10.
6) Suggested contract language for UK Addendum: we will propose a short clause documenting routing fallback and customer-level residency pins. If Helix needs the UK IDTA signature path, we can produce the addendum and a DocuSign link.

Caveats/notes:
- Onshore-cache fallback: we will describe the fallback as a transient caching behavior enforced by TTLs and explicit KV wipe on session termination. If Helix requires persistent residency guarantees, that becomes a product-level residency pin and needs separate procurement.
- Subprocessor changes after signing: we can provide a 30-day notification cadence or an option for monthly rolled-up attestations for critical subprocessors.

Next steps:
- Please confirm if you want the SOC2 excerpt under NDA (we'll send a one-click NDA).
- Confirm whether Helix expects the onshore-cache fallback to be an acceptable transfer safeguard or whether you require an alternative (e.g., guaranteed EU-only pins).

I will start the draft SCC/IDTA matrix and the site-processing diagram and share by Tuesday COB (Day 3).

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
